abstract_html: We prove a product formula for the universal series of effective one-cycles on a smooth projective threefold X with trivial canonical bundle and H1(X,𝒪X)=H2(X,𝒪X)=0. The identity holds in Pardon's rational cycle algebra. Its genus-g factor is defined by the circle with opposite weights on two line bundles of degree g−1 whose tensor product is the canonical bundle of the curve. The exponents are the elementary-cluster integers of Ionel and Parker, with finite genus support in each integral curve class. We construct these integers as signed multiplicities in a decomposition of the cycles on X. In the algebra formed from almost-complex families, a deformation on the sum of two copies of a spin line identifies each antidiagonal class with the point class of the corresponding multiple of an elementary curve. Excision for disconnected cycles factors the image of the series of X at each energy bound. Stable maps of fixed genus distinguish the multiplicity-one classes, which suffices to lift the product to the complex cycle algebra.
